repo_prior_art.cite: none; the closest banked ExactID work, eid_lp_svar_nonequiv, concerns LP/SVAR impulse-response non-equivalence rather than covariance-environment replacement.

published_prior_art.cite: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 is the all-honest iff criterion; AkhavanEtAl2019GeometryJD and ShenEtAl2020RJDSEM give robust-JD procedures, not an exact worst-case whole-slot replacement radius with a legal BACKSHIFT converse.

RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Corollary 2(ii), gives generic all-continuous identifiability, while PerryVonKugelgenScholkopf2022SparseShift studies sparse mechanism changes rather than the stated affine-occupancy formula under whole-slot replacement.

AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID motivates identification-robust confidence sets, but the displayed coverage inclusion is a direct BACKSHIFT compatibility-union construction rather than a distinct inference frontier.

Afsari2008JDSensitivity treats local sensitivity for a selected joint-diagonalization family, and AndrewsCheng2013SporadicID treats general sporadic-identification inference; neither supplies rational affine-minor certificates or subset-uniform BACKSHIFT contraction.

soundness_flags.label: prop:confidence-union-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: Coverage follows directly by choosing true honest-slot covariances and arbitrary points from the nonempty corrupted-slot regions in the defining union, so this should be a definition-level corollary rather than a root theorem target.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-replacement-radius / ass:invariant-noise-interior
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The legal converse is asserted only on the interior invariant-noise class Ω ∈ S++p, not on the full PSD-noise BACKSHIFT class.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Exact replacement radius conditional on Ω ∈ S++p; the c=0 BACKSHIFT comparison is only a restricted sanity reduction.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: def:subset-consensus and oeq:certified-uniform-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Subset enumeration assumes a full-solution feasibility oracle and does not supply a terminating implementable solver.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Only the oracle reduction is settled; certified feasibility, quantitative contraction, and weak-minor abstention remain the open target.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 3, equations (5)-(10); p. 4, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines covariance-difference joint diagonalization with unit diagonal and cycle-product normalization, proves unique population recovery iff its pairwise intervention-variance determinant condition holds, and gives generic identifiability for at least three continuously randomized environments.

source_verification_receipts.version: IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information Processing over Networks 6, 2020
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 5, Section III.C, equations (27)-(28); p. 6, Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: R-JDSEM uses an ℓ1 objective for sparse outlier components in local covariance matrices, while its identifiability theorem assumes a directed-network SEM with Kruskal-rank and known-edge conditions rather than whole-environment replacement.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 4.2 and equation (42) as cited in the proposal
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article proposes geometry-based approximate joint diagonalization and an outlier-omission procedure, not a necessary-and-sufficient adversarial covariance-slot identification radius.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 4, Corollary 4.2; p. 6, Theorem 5.3 and Corollary 5.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves bivariate and high-probability DAG identifiability under probabilistic sparse mechanism shifts, not affine occupancy or adversarial covariance-slot replacement.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1111.7088 author version; cited IEEE journal version not directly inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible version gives exact non-unitary joint-diagonalizer uniqueness conditions for a fixed diagonal family through diagonal-profile collinearity; no primary-version formula mismatch is asserted.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2007.14034 author version corresponding to SIAM JMAA 43(2), 2022
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 7 characterizes simultaneous diagonalization by congruence of a complete Hermitian family through an equivalent positive-definite feasibility system.

source_verification_receipts.version: Cowles Discussion Paper 1824R, revised 2012; the cited Journal of Econometrics version was not directly inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible version studies estimation, testing, and confidence procedures under sporadic identification failure; it is a general inference comparator rather than a corrupted-BACKSHIFT subset-inversion result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Move prop:confidence-union-coverage into the confidence-union definition or a sanity-corollary paragraph, and retain the certificate/modulus problem as the only inference-level root target.

Separate the uniqueness direction, which may retain the PSD invariant-noise class, from the SPD-only legal-converse construction and state explicitly whether a PSD-boundary converse is an open extension.
Add a worked sparse support design at m=2c+3 for p≥3 that lists all pairwise incidence counts, computes Mgen, and verifies the claimed threshold constructively.

recommended_next_step: Revise by demoting the direct confidence-union inclusion to a definitional corollary, then advance the conditional field-tier radius and sparse-support kernels to Stage 0.
